days.label: Monday
days.text: Monday itself has more going on than a rainy start suggests. The Humane Society of Chittenden County tees off its Putts for Paws charity golf tournament at Vermont National in South Burlington, running 11 to 6:30. Downtown, there is a free community screening of The Alabama Solution at 6:30 in the Film House at Main Street Landing, the Academy Award nominated documentary, brought to town by a host who reached out to the filmmakers for permission to screen it. Anime fans convene at Anime Group at Pathways Vermont's Morgan's Place from 6 to 8, Spanish speakers of every level get Spanish Chat Mondays at 7, meeting this first Monday at Ben & Jerry's on Church Street, and trivia people can take their pick in Winooski, where the Monkey House and McKee's Original both run free games at 7.

days.label: Tuesday
days.text: Tuesday belongs to Essex Junction, where the police department hosts National Night Out at Essex High School starting at 5, a free community night of safety demos, youth events, exhibits, music and a hot dog cookout. Early birds can hit the first Tech Breakfast of a new monthly series at Zero Gravity from 8 to 10, or the networking coffee for women at Hula at 8:30. In the evening, Secretary of State Sarah Copeland Hanzas takes questions at a free conversation at Fletcher Free Library at 6:30, registration required. The Lake Monsters host Summer of Love Night at Centennial Field, tie dye jerseys on the field and a poster giveaway for the first 500 fans, first pitch 6:35. And Ohio folk trio Oliver Hazard plays the Showcase Lounge at 8, a band that won a Facebook raffle to record one song and cut their whole debut album in a single take instead.

days.label: Wednesday
days.text: Wednesday opens the big one. The 46th annual Sidewalk Sale takes over Church Street Marketplace starting Wednesday and running through Sunday, five days of deals up and down the bricks. Cyclists can join a 9 mile evening ride from Switchback [MEETUP] at 5:30, a flat out and back to Leddy Park that lands at the taproom for burger night. My weekly Pick-up Basketball [MEETUP] run goes 5:30 to 7:30 at Pomeroy Park, come get in a game. The South End Walk/Bike Forum runs 5 to 7 at Public Works on Pine Street, where the city and Local Motion want to hear what your walk or ride actually needs. At night, VTIFF screens the 1916 silent western Hell's Hinges with a live improvised score at 7 in the Screening Room at 60 Lake Street, and the Craftsbury Chamber Players continue a summer run they have kept up every year since 1966, at 7:30 at Elley-Long in Colchester.

days.label: Thursday
days.text: Thursday is absolutely packed. Party on the Bricks pops up at Halvorson's from 5:30 to 8 with the Green Kettle Band, free dancing in the street in the middle of Sidewalk Sale week. Our group heads to Lake Monsters Baseball & Creemee Night [MEETUP] at Centennial Field, where the team becomes the Vermont Creemees for the night with creemee trucks on the concourse, first pitch 6:35. Williston gets a free Beatles tribute on the green at Maple Tree Place at 6, South Burlington runs SB Nite Out at Veterans Memorial Park at 5:30 with Jenni Johnson & The Junketeers, and crafters can bring whatever project needs finishing to Crafting in Community [MEETUP] in Essex Junction at 6:30. Curious types have a full menu too. Shelburne Farms hosts a free pasture walk with a UVM field naturalist from 5 to 7, the Media Factory teaches Camera Essentials at 6 for anyone stuck on auto mode, and Annie Caswell's retrospective opens with a reception from 4 to 7 at the Winemakers Gallery in Shelburne. Night owls can finish at VTIFF's screening of Spike Lee's debut She's Gotta Have It at 7, catch The Babies' improv variety show at Vermont Comedy Club at 7 ($5, students free), or settle in at Radio Bean for the Compa & Friends residency at 8:30. Early risers can even give back first, with the BTV Cleanup Crew meeting at Kru Coffee at 7:30 AM to sweep Church Street and the parks.
